subject: Evidence request: CI role bindings, PR approval gates, and emergency change trail
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@northbridge.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@trustassure.com
Date: Sat, 1 Jun 2029 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Request: CI / PR / emergency change evidence for SIG questionnaire

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for taking our SIG questionnaire. A couple of clarifications came up from our security team: they want concrete artifacts showing (1) who can change CI pipeline definitions (role bindings), (2) PR approval gating for protected branches (who approves and what SLOs), and (3) audit trail for emergency/urgent change approvals and rollbacks in the last 12 months.

Can you provide: a spreadsheet or CSV mapping CI pipeline service accounts and group role bindings; a short PDF that annotates your PR approval policy with samples of enforced checks from the last 3 months; and the emergency change log entries (redacted if needed) that show who authorized and who performed the emergency deploy and the rollback if applicable.

We'd like this by EOD Wednesday (US pacific) if possible so our assessor can incorporate into the SIG review. Happy to take a short screen-share to walk through the artifacts if that's easier.

Regards,
Nina
Nina Patel
Security QA Lead — Northbridge Financial

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@northbridge.com>
Cc: audit@trustassure.com, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 2 Jun 2029 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: CI / PR / emergency change evidence for SIG questionnaire

Nina —

Thanks for the note. Looping in Marissa (Engineering Manager, Platform) and Karthik (Head of Release Reliability) to pull the artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Role bindings: pipeline definitions are managed in Git (infra/repos/ci-config). Changes to pipeline YAMLs require PRs against the repo; only members of the "platform-pipeline-admins" Google group and owners of the repo can merge into the main branch. We'll export the IAM bindings and include the CSV.

- PR approvals: we enforce CODEOWNERS + required reviewers (2) on protected branches, a CI success gate (unit + lint + static analysis), and an approval from an engineer in the release rotation for production-impacting changes. We'll create an annotated PDF showing policy excerpts and two recent PRs that exercised the gate.

- Emergency changes: we have an emergency-change policy requiring (a) PagerDuty incident ticket, (b) documented emergency PR with "emergency/*" prefix, (c) escalation approval via the on-call director (Slack + email), and (d) a post-facto RFC within 72 hours. We will export the change log entries for the last 12 months with PII redacted.

Deliverables we will attach: ci-role-bindings-20290603.csv, pr-approval-policy-annotated.pdf, emergency-change-log-202905.json. If you prefer a walkthrough, Marissa can demo the repo history and Karthik can show the audit exports via our internal tooling.

Will deliver by EOD Wed PST and will post a Drive link to the folder here when ready.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Head of Platform Security Programs
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@northbridge.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@trustassure.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: CI / PR / emergency change evidence for SIG questionnaire

Hi Nina —

Attachments are prepared and linked below. Short notes on each:

1) ci-role-bindings-20290603.csv (attached) — columns: resource,path,role,member,last_modified_by,last_modified_at. I exported the Cloud IAM bindings for the CI runner service account(s) and combined them with our GitHub team mappings for repo write/maintain permissions. We added a "notes" column indicating why a binding exists (e.g., cross-account deploy job).

2) pr-approval-policy-annotated.pdf (attached) — annotated snapshot from our CODEOWNERS + branch protection settings with two sample PRs (PR# 4829 and PR# 4987). The PDF highlights the enforced checks: 2 required reviewers, block on merge if CI fails, and an explicit production-impact label that triggers the release-rotation approval. The two sample PRs show the approvals and CI timestamps.

3) emergency-change-log-202905.json (attached) — sanitized entries for the three emergency changes in the last 12 months: 2028-11-14 (hotfix DB migration rollback), 2029-02-09 (urgent perf patch), 2029-04-21 (security patch with immediate deploy). Each entry includes: incident id, on-call approver, acting engineer, PR link, deploy job id, and rollback job id where applicable. All PII removed per our policy.

If you'd like I can do a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow 10am PST to show the logs and answer any questions. Otherwise, please confirm receipt and whether these meet the SIG assessor's needs.

Attachments: ci-role-bindings-20290603.csv; pr-approval-policy-annotated.pdf; emergency-change-log-202905.json

Best,
Marissa Cole
Engineering Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: audit@trustassure.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: nina.patel@northbridge.com
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: CI / PR / emergency change evidence for SIG questionnaire

Marissa / Jordan —

Got the artifacts, thank you. Quick review looks good; the CSV maps cleanly to the IAM exports and the annotated PDF shows the branch protection enforcement and two representative PRs. The emergency-change log has sufficient fields and redaction is appropriate. Two small follow-ups before we close this item: (1) can you provide the commit SHAs that correspond to the last three emergency deploys (we need a cross-check against the deploy system), and (2) can you confirm the retention policy for pipeline logs and audit exports (retention period + location)?

If you can drop those two items in the same Drive folder by EOD Tuesday we'll be able to finalize the SIG evidence pack. Otherwise we may ask for a short call.

Thanks,
TrustAssure — Evidence Review Team
